title: ARTS, PARKS, AND CITY FACILITIES and BUDGET AND FINANCE COMMITTEES' REPORT relative to the Third Construction Projects Report for Fiscal Year (FY) 2026-27.…
text:
[Council File 26-1124-S2]
[Items for which Public Hearings Have Not Been Held - (10 Votes Required for Consideration)]
ARTS, PARKS, AND CITY FACILITIES and BUDGET AND FINANCE COMMITTEES' REPORT relative to the Third Construction Projects Report for Fiscal Year (FY) 2026-27. A. Arts, Parks, and City Facilities Committee Report Recommendations for Council action, SUBJECT TO THE APPROVAL OF THE MAYOR:
1. AUTHORIZE the Controller to transfer $5,457,297 between departments and funds as specified in Attachment 1 of the City Administrative Officer (CAO) report dated October 29, 2026, attached to Council file No. 26-1124-S2.
2. AUTHORIZE the Controller to transfer $45,851 between accounts within departments and funds as specified in Attachment 2 of said CAO report.
3. In accordance with Recommendation No. 1 above, AUTHORIZE the Controller to reimburse the General Fund within the Municipal Improvement Corporation of Los Angeles (MICLA), upon CAO approval and receipt of the department requesting labor services, construction materials, and supply invoices for completed work, to include reimbursement for labor services documentation that must contain an hourly breakdown with task descriptions and codes detailing the completed MICLA eligible work, relative to the departmental accounts designated for the following projects:
a. CAO - Space Optimization Mangrove Building - Cabling Expansion Project (Item E)
b. Department of Cultural Affairs - Nate Holden Theater Improvements (Item H)
c. Los Angeles Zoo - Sea Life Cliff Holding Pools Liner and Flooring Replacement (Item Z).
4. INSTRUCT the Bureau of Engineering, relative to the Fire Station No. 31 (Sylmar) project, to:
a. Submit as part of the 2027-28 Capital Technology Improvement Expenditure Program (CTIEP), a MICLA funding request for the project’s construction under the continuing/ongoing CTIEP projects category.
b. Submit an updated expenditure plan for previously allocated and unspent MICLA funds to determine if any unspent MICLA funds from pre-development and design services can be reallocated towards site improvement and construction mobilization work to reduce the new MICLA request (Item A).
5. RESCIND Item H in the 2026-27 Second Construction Projects Report dated October 5, 2026, attached to Council file No. 26-1124-S1, to be replaced by Item C in said CAO report dated October 29, 2026.
6. REAUTHORIZE the use of up to $1,204,358 in 2023-24 MICLA funding authority (Fund No. 298/40, Account No. 40Y20L - Space Optimization Tenant Work) that has expired; and, AUTHORIZE the continued use of these funds beyond the City’s MICLA Three-Year Spending Policy (Item E).
7. REAUTHORIZE the use of up to $1,250,000 in 2023-24 MICLA funding authority (Fund No. 298/50, Account No. 50YPCC - Harbor City Recreation Center Outdoor Restrooms) that has expired; and, AUTHORIZE the continued use of these funds beyond the City’s MICLA Three-Year Spending Policy (Item I).
8. REAUTHORIZE the use of up to $113,822 in 2023-24 MICLA funding authority (Fund No. 298/40, Account No. 40Y24P - Fuel Management System Upgrade - Phase II) that has expired; and, AUTHORIZE the continued use of these funds beyond the City’s MICLA Three-Year Spending Policy (Item Q).
9. REAUTHORIZE the use of up to $597,360 in 2022-23 MICLA funding authority (Fund No. 298/40, Account No. 40W24P - Fuel Management System Upgrade - Phase II) that has expired; and, AUTHORIZE the continued use of these funds beyond the City’s MICLA Three-Year Spending Policy (Item R).
10. AUTHORIZE to reprogram MICLA funds from Los Angeles Fire Department equipment purchases adopted in the 2026-27 Adopted Budget to purchase replacement vehicles (Item S).
11. REAUTHORIZE a total of $2,000,000 in MICLA funding included in the 2026-27 Adopted Budget for the Los Angeles Zoo - Capital Program (Item Y).
12. AUTHORIZE to reprogram and appropriate $250,000 in CTIEP funds to the Department of Building and Safety’s Repair and Demolition Fund to address nuisance abatement at private properties (Item BB).
13. AUTHORIZE the CAO to make technical corrections, as necessary, to the transactions authorized through said CAO report dated October 29, 2026, as required to implement the intent of those transactions. B. Budget and Finance Committee Report Recommendations for Council action, SUBJECT TO THE APPROVAL OF THE MAYOR:
CONCUR with the Arts, Parks, and City Facilities Committee's action of November 4, 2026 to approve the recommendations contained in the City Administrative Officer (CAO) report dated October 29, 2026, attached to the Council file.
Fiscal Impact Statement:
The CAO reports that the recommendations stated in the report include transfers, appropriations, and authority for expenditures totaling $5.5 million. This consists of $1.2 million from various special funds, $1.4 million in MICLA funds, $1.6 million in CTIEP funds, and $1.3 million in General funds. All transfers and appropriations are based on existing funds, reimbursements, or revenues. There is an unanticipated General Fund impact in an amount not yet determined for operations and maintenance costs of the Warner Grand Theatre. These costs will be addressed through the City budget process at the time the facility is scheduled for completion.
Debt impact statement The CAO reports that the issuance of MICLA debt is a General Fund obligation. The proposed MICLA funding for the capital improvement projects (Items E, I, Q, R, and Y) would cause the City to borrow $5.2 million at an approximate 5.5 percent interest rate over a period of 20 years. The total estimated debt service for these MICLA- funded projects is $8.6 million, including interest of approximately $3.5 million. The estimated average annual debt service is $0.4 million over a period of 20 years. Actual interest rates may differ as rates are dependent on market conditions at the time of issuance. The CAO's Office cannot fully predict what interest rates will be in the future. In accordance with the City's Debt Management Policy, the City has an established debt ceiling to guide the evaluation of the affordability for future debt. The debt ceiling, for non-voted direct debt as a percentage of General Fund revenues, is six percent. The 2026-27 non-voter-approved debt service ratio is 2.40 percent. The issuance of MICLA debt for these projects will not cause the City to exceed the six percent non-voter-approved debt limit. Financial policies The CAO reports that the recommendations stated in the report comply with the statement City’s Financial Policies in that appropriations for funds are limited to available cash balances needed to fund ongoing maintenance, programming, project shortfalls, and critical repairs or operational needs in the current budget year.
Community Impact Statement:
None submitted
summary: The City Administrative Officer's third construction projects report for fiscal 2026-27, which is also referred to the Budget and Finance Committee.
